title: Exact module pullback and diagonal tensor for internal restriction
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small site $(C,J)$ with finite limits [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$. For a sheaf of groups $K$ with $\mathcal V$-small values, let $\mathscr E^K$ be the category of sheaves of sets $X$ with a natural left action $K\times X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws; its maps are equivariant sheaf maps. Let $L$ be a sheaf of groups, $\theta:L\to K$ a group-sheaf morphism, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Write $I_K$ for trivial action, $\operatorname{Res}_\theta$ for action restriction, and $R_K=I_KR$. Suppose geometric morphisms $p_K:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E$ and $q_\theta:\mathscr E^L\to\mathscr E^K$ have these inverse images and identity structural ring maps [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Via the sectionwise action-site module equivalence [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], their canonical module pullbacks [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] identify naturally with trivial inflation and restriction of equivariant $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For either pullback $f^*$ the identification $f^*M=(f^{-1}R)\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M\simeq f^{-1}M$ sends $r\otimes m$ to $rm$ and has inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$; the underlying map on module morphisms is unchanged. Both functors are additive and preserve kernels and cokernels, whose underlying sheaves are respectively sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels; hence both are exact. The sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] corresponds to the base sheaf tensor with diagonal action $a(x\otimes y)=ax\otimes ay$. For $p_K^*$ and $q_\theta^*$ the canonical comparisons $f^*M\otimes f^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*(M\otimes N)$ are induced by the identity on presheaf pure tensors $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$, followed by module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Their unit comparisons are the identity on the regular coefficient ring. These tensor comparisons are natural and satisfy the associativity, symmetry and unit coherence equations.
